div.div: The "Fairness" calculation: It tracks how much time each process has spent on the CPU. Processes that have had less time get higher priority for the next available cycle.

path.style: stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: In a "noisy neighbor" scenario where three pods are fighting for a single CPU core, Kubernetes uses CPU Shares (derived from your requests) to decide who wins.

path.style: stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));
fill: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Requests = Priority: Your cpu: 1000m request is converted into 1024 shares.

div.div: The Web Service (1024 shares) is guaranteed 2/3 of the CPU time.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 118px; height: 1px; padding-top: 290px; margin-left: 1371px;

div.div: The Batch Job (512 shares) is guaranteed 1/3 of the CPU time

path.style: stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));
fill: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));
stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: If the Web Service is idle, the Batch Job can "steal" the unused CPU. But the moment the Web Service wakes up, the Batch Job is compressed back down to its 1/3 share.

div.div:
Throttling: The 100ms Quota Window:
Throttling is the "speed limit" enforced by the kernel. It works on a 100ms period by default.

path.style: stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));
fill: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 233px; height: 1px; padding-top: 510px; margin-left: 816px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Example: You have a limit of 0.5 CPU (500m). This gives you 50ms of execution time every 100ms.

path.style: stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));
fill: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 358px; height: 1px; padding-top: 780px; margin-left: 841px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: The Sprint: If your app is multi-threaded and uses all 50ms in the first 10ms of the window, it is instantly frozen for the remaining 90ms.

path.style: stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));
fill: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: The Wait: Even if the physical CPU on the node is 90% idle, your app cannot run until the next 100ms window starts.

div.div:
The Impact: Latency Jitter:
Because throttling stops and starts your app in tiny bursts, it creates "Jitter"—inconsistent response times.

div.div:
Throttled:
App is frozen mid-calculation. Request takes ~100ms (10ms work + ~90ms wait).

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: Your "Average Latency" might look okay, but your P99 Latency (the worst cases) will spike wildly.
